Title: Manager - Software Engineering
Description:
**Job Description Summary**
This role is accountable for L4 escalation outcomes across the AIS Digital Verisound and Imaging 360 product family. It covers complex customer escalations, defect triage and resolution, root cause analysis, and reducing recurring issues through improved observability, monitoring and permanent fixes.
  
  
The role also builds technical capability across L4 engineers, product experts and L3 support through training, knowledge sharing and consistent processes. It works with Engineering, Product, Architecture, Quality and Regulatory, Cybersecurity and Services to resolve issues on time and to scale support as the portfolio and installed base grow.
  
  
**Job Description**
Roles and responsibilities
  
  
Own L4 escalation outcomes
  
  

* Evaluate incidents raised by L3, confirm they are valid production issues, and assign each to the right L4 engineer by product and region, with a named owner until closure.
* Reproduce, debug and resolve complex and high-severity issues across the stack: application code, logs, databases, cloud services, networking and integrations.
* Settle severity and priority disagreements with L3 and remove cross-functional blockers.
* Drive resolution within severity-based targets, with disciplined management of cases on hold.

Reduce escalations at the source
  
  

* Improve observability, monitoring and alerting so problems are detected and diagnosed before customers report them.
* Work with Engineering to fix recurring issues at the root cause.
* Automate diagnostics, routine fixes and runbooks to cut manual effort and time to resolve.
* Define, design and implement benchmarks to catch performance regressions and bottlenecks. Agree acceptable performance parameters with Product Management and run performance and scalability testing across the tech stack.

Drive quality and reliability
  
  

* Hands on and lead defect triage and resolution. Make sure confirmed defects are recorded in the defect systems and classified with Engineering and the design review board.
* Lead root cause analysis for high-severity and recurring issues, and track preventive actions to completion.
* Spot trends across products (defect inflow, recurring issues, reopened cases) and feed them back to Product, Architecture and Engineering.

Build team capability
  
  

* Develop and deliver technical training on products, architecture and troubleshooting for L4 engineers, product experts and L3 support.
* Provide technical guidance on complex cases and review RCAs.
* Build and maintain a searchable knowledge base, short how-to articles and a list of top recurring issues and their fixes.
* Run a weekly knowledge-transfer session with L3 so more issues are resolved before they reach L4.
* Maintain onboarding material for new team members and support succession planning.
* Serve as a best-practice and quality resource and stay current on technical developments in the area.

Build the operating model
  
  

* Establish one consistent L4 process across all product lines, with a single RACI, RCA standard and KPI set.
* Define and report metrics such as mean time to resolve, aged cases, hold time, reopen rate, recurring issues and volume by product and region.
* Define the coverage model (regions, backups and high-severity response) and plan capacity as the installed base grows.

Communicate and govern
  
  

* Be the single voice for external and stakeholder communication on L4 escalations, with a consistent update cadence by severity, and provide US time zone leadership.
* Own the weekly operating rhythm: the stakeholder report and the program review of SLA, new, on-hold and resolved cases, flagging items that need leadership help or a decision.
* Explain difficult or sensitive technical information clearly and build consensus across functions.

Work responsibly in a regulated environment
  
  

* Make sure incidents with possible patient-safety implications are documented and routed to the owning channels under established procedures.
* Follow applicable quality, security and privacy requirements, and keep team training and required compliance current.

Scope and judgment
  
  

* Uses judgment to solve moderately complex technical and operational problems, takes new perspectives on existing solutions, and uses data analysis to support recommendations.
* Has in-depth knowledge of best practices and how the area integrates with others, and contributes to strategy and policy for L4 and reliability engineering.
* Leads small projects with moderate risk and resource needs, and acts as a resource for less experienced colleagues.

**Required Qualifications**

* Master’s degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma / GED with at least 6 years of experience in the Job Family Group or Function).
* Experience in site reliability, sustaining engineering or production support of complex software products, including cloud or SaaS products.
* Troubleshooting and debugging skills across application code, logs, databases, cloud services and networking.
* Track record of managing escalations, root cause analysis, and defect triage and resolution.
* Experience training or mentoring engineers.
* Experience with incident management tools (for example ServiceNow) and defect tracking systems.
* Clear communication with technical and executive audiences under pressure; comfortable working across time zones.

Desired characteristics
  
  

* 6 or more years in software engineering, site reliability or sustaining engineering.
* Medical device or other regulated software experience (for example FDA, ISO 13485 and IEC 62304 practices).
* Experience with observability and monitoring tools (for example Splunk, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus or ELK) and with AWS or Azure.
* Scripting and automation skills (for example Python, PowerShell or Bash).
* Familiarity with imaging or digital fleet products, DevOps practices and cybersecurity.
* Experience developing training material or knowledge bases.
* ITIL or similar service-management knowledge; Lean and Heartbeat problem-solving.
* Strong oral and written communication, interpersonal and leadership skills; proven ability to analyze and resolve problems, and to plan, document and execute programs. Established project management skills.

Title: Director of Data Architecture
Description:
Supplier.io is the data foundation that enterprises build their supplier decisions on. Fragmented, duplicated, and unreliable supplier data quietly limits the ROI of source-to-pay platforms, analytics, risk, and AI initiatives, so we resolve, enrich, and continuously maintain the industry's most complete supplier identity, then put it to work for the teams that buy and the suppliers themselves. Relied on by companies across the Fortune 2000 for accurate data, our platform helps corporate procurement, finance, and compliance teams manage their vendor master, source diverse and sustainable suppliers, and mitigate risk, all from one verified identity instead of a dozen disconnected systems.  
  
Our solutions turn that foundation into action: accurate data and continuous maintenance for teams managing a fragmented vendor master, sourcing intelligence built resolving even the hardest-to-identify suppliers, small, local, and diverse businesses, for teams tracking sustainability and compliance, and direct visibility for the suppliers themselves into where they stand with the enterprises that buy from them. Whether you're resolving vendor records, sourcing alternatives, or measuring program results, Supplier.io transforms complexity into clarity, so teams can lead with confidence and build supply chains that deliver for both business and community.  
  
For more information, visit www.supplier.io.

**The Opportunity**

The Director, Data Architecture owns the strategy, standards, and team behind how data moves through Supplier.io, from source systems and web-scraping pipelines through ingestion, transformation, and governed delivery into the warehouses and marts the rest of the business relies on. You'll operate as a peer to our other engineering leaders, setting data architecture direction jointly with the CTO, while staying accountable for the reliability, quality, and governance of every data workflow we run.

You'll lead two distinct groups: a Data Engineering team building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and a Data Operations Engineering team running and maintaining the processes already in production. In the near term, before the team and its processes are fully built out, this role is hands-on: you'll be designing pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly, not just directing from a distance.

**What You Will Do**

**Data Architecture & Platform Strategy**

* Own the multi-year data architecture strategy across our data warehouses and operational data stores, including evolving toward a medallion (bronze, silver, gold) lakehouse model.
* Design and own our data lake and warehouse architecture, including the formation and population of data marts that serve analytics, product, and stakeholder reporting needs.
* Set the orchestration strategy and standards for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT, and automated workflow management, and standardize the tooling used across the function.
* Own the infrastructure and administration behind our data warehouses and pipelines, including capacity, reliability, and cost.
* Own data governance end to end: the policies, standards, and practices for data quality, lineage, access, retention, and classification across every system of record.

**Team & Execution Leadership**

* Build, lead, and grow two functions: Data Engineering, building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, running and maintaining existing production data processes.
* Decide how the function is organized as it scales, including when and whether to add management layers beneath you to run day-to-day execution.
* Stay hands-on early: design and review pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly until the team is built out to carry that execution independently, and stay close enough to the technology afterward to make credible architecture calls.

**Cross-Functional Partnership**

* Partner with engineering leadership to keep data architecture decisions aligned with company-wide standards.
* Work closely with data engineering teams on technical planning and delivery for our core data products.
* Partner with product, analytics, and other business stakeholders across the company to understand data needs and translate them into warehouse and data mart designs.

**Data Quality & Compliance**

* Define and enforce data quality gates, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
* Own data access controls, classification, and retention policy across the data estate.
* Ensure compliance-relevant and audit-sensitive data is handled according to governance standards as our data sources and customer base grow.

**What You Will Need to Succeed**

* 10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, including 5+ years in a Director or Manager-level leadership role owning architecture strategy and a team, not just individual delivery.
* Deep, hands-on experience designing and operating cloud data warehouse or lakehouse architectures (Snowflake and/or BigQuery), including medallion (bronze, silver, gold) patterns.
* Experience integrating a range of source systems (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and building ingestion and ETL pipelines from varied and unstructured sources, including web-scraping pipelines and background job orchestration.
* A track record of building and scaling a data engineering or data platform organization, including deciding when and how to split engineering and operations functions.
* Strong data governance background: establishing policies and standards for data quality, lineage, access, and retention in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment.
* Experience setting technical direction jointly with peer engineering leaders and influencing architecture decisions across teams.
* Excellent communication skills, comfortable setting strategy with peer leaders and reporting data platform health, cost, and risk directly to the CTO.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience consolidating or re-architecting data platforms following an acquisition or significant data source expansion.
* Experience with orchestration tooling such as Airflow or dbt, and with scraping or crawling infrastructure at scale.
* Background establishing data marts and self-service analytics layers for non-engineering stakeholders.
* Familiarity with data observability tooling (Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar).

Title: Senior Program Manager, Strategy and Expansion, MEATR DSP Strategy, Planning and Expansion
Description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Customers want what they need in minutes, not days. Join Amazon's Last Mile team in the Middle East, Africa and Turkey to shape how our fastest delivery services, including Amazon Now and Amazon Rush, grow and run for customers, delivery associates, Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) and Amazon.  
  
As Senior Program Manager, you will own and lead the strategic programmes that set how our Speed last mile network runs across the region. At the core is flexible capacity: designing models that let DSP capacity move up and down with demand, setting how they fit into annual and weekly planning, and getting Operations, Finance, People teams and DSP partners behind them. Your portfolio may also cover partner commercials, compliance and training, and it will change as priorities change.  
  
Many problems won't arrive well defined. You will frame them, find the ones worth solving, align senior stakeholders on a path forward and build mechanisms that make the answers scale across countries. You will also help shape the team's wider strategy and roadmap.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Set the strategy: own the multi-year capacity and growth plan for Quick Commerce and Speed, and the region's input to annual planning.
* Plan capacity: within the regional plan, build short, mid and long range plans that match DSP and delivery associate supply to demand by hour, day and season.
* Build flexible capacity: design, launch and scale flexible models alongside the fixed DSP network, with the operating, commercial and compliance framework to run them.
* Grow the channel: launch new cities, stores and countries with capacity ready before go-live.
* Improve efficiency: raise utilisation and lower cost per delivery without moving cost onto DSPs or associates.
* Build partner economics: shape DSP commercial models with Finance that work at every volume level, and lead the trade-off decisions.
* Look after delivery associates: design fair, safe, compliant schedules and lead the regional response to labour rule changes.
* Align and lead change: bring Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Tech and DSPs behind one plan, and run readiness and approvals.
* Build mechanisms: set planning tool requirements with Tech, and the metrics, guardrails and reviews that run the channel, using automation and AI.
* Lead and write: influence senior leaders, mentor PMs and analysts, and write documents that drive decisions.

  
A day in the life  
You start with yesterday's Quick Commerce and Speed performance: where capacity matched demand, where routes ran short or associates sat idle, and what it cost. Mid-morning, you join the weekly planning review to agree where flexible capacity steps in next week. You then meet a DSP owner to test a new flexible model against their margin and their associates' hours. After lunch, you work with Finance and Legal on the case for scaling it to a second country. You end the day writing for senior leaders: what the pilot showed, what you recommend and what you need from them.  
  
About the team  
This is a new role reporting to the Senior Manager, Strategy and Expansion, MEATr DSP. Quick Commerce and Speed, including Amazon Now and Amazon Rush, are delivered by DSPs, and flexible capacity is a lead theme in the region's 2027 plan. You will own Speed capacity and flexible capacity programmes across the region, planning inside the regional capacity plan and working with the Network Optimisation team, who own rate cards. You will mentor PMs and analysts and write planning papers reviewed at Director and VP level.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 2+ years of program or project management experience
* Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
* Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
* Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
* Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

Title: Senior Manager, Fulfillment
Description:
**Who We Are**

Chomps is America's fastest-growing meat snack brand, redefining convenient snacking with a commitment to real ingredients and bold, satisfying flavors. Crafted from 100% grass-fed, grass-finished beef and venison, along with antibiotic-free turkey and chicken, each Chomps meat stick delivers 10+ grams of high-quality protein without sugar, hormones, soy, dairy, artificial preservatives, artificial nitrates, or MSG. Seasoned with a blend of flavorful herbs and spices, Chomps provides a nutritious protein snack for the whole family. As a minority-owned, family-operated, and B Corporation-certified business, Chomps prioritizes thoughtful sourcing and recently earned the non–ultra-processed food certification through the non-GMO project. Discover a new standard in snacking at www.chomps.com.

**Traits of a Chompian**

If you've been called nimble, resourceful, and persistent, then you might just be a Chompian. You're a team player who's self-motivated and action-oriented. You're committed to delivering efficiency and accuracy, and you happen to be great at proactive cross-functional communication. You're a critical thinker and a natural problem solver who enjoys details, research, and data. You take initiative and complete ownership of everything you do, and you'll go the extra mile for your team, consumers, and audience. You're hungry to learn with a passion to grow and improve every day. You also take a keen interest in health, fitness, and nutrition. Sound like you? Then we want to meat you.

**What You Will Do**

The Senior Manager, Fulfillment is responsible for managing day-to-day fulfillment execution and the customer service function to ensure Chomps' fulfillment network operates with accuracy, accountability, cost discipline, and scalability. This role translates established fulfillment priorities into clear operating routines and partner expectations across multiple distribution locations and 3PL partners. The ideal candidate brings strong fulfillment and 3PL management experience, understands order execution and customer service operations, and can turn complex operational priorities into practical processes, measurable results, and clear cross-functional communication.

**Role Expectations:** This role is expected to independently manage recurring fulfillment and customer service cadences, 3PL partner follow-up, KPI reporting, process controls, order exception management, and customer escalations. This role will also provide operational inputs, data analysis, customer and service insights, risk visibility, and execution support to leadership for network planning, budget development, partner governance, and material service, cost, compliance, or performance escalations.

**Responsibilities**

* **Fulfillment Network Operations & 3PL Management**
  + Support daily fulfillment operations across a growing multi-node distribution network, ensuring accurate order execution, capacity readiness, inventory flow, cost discipline, and consistent partner follow-through.
  + Manage weekly and monthly 3PL operating cadences, including partner meetings, KPI reviews, action-item tracking, QBR content preparation, performance follow-up, corrective action tracking, SLA monitoring, root-cause analysis, and readiness checkpoints.
  + Create, maintain, and continuously improve scalable SOPs, process controls, compliance requirements, and partner playbooks covering receiving, inventory control, order release, allocation, pick/pack/ship execution, exception management, and partner escalation paths, ensuring consistent execution across distribution nodes and customer channels.
  + Support fulfillment budget management by preparing invoice audits, spend analysis, productivity tracking, cost-per-order or cost-per-case reporting, and cost-reduction recommendations across the partner network.
* **Order Management & Allocation**
  + Manage order allocation across wholesale, retail, eCommerce, and other channels, balancing customer requirements, inventory availability, freight efficiency, production constraints, and service commitments.
  + Partner with Sales, Planning, Transportation, Finance, Customer Supply Chain, and Operations to execute customer requirements, manage order flow constraints, support inventory positioning decisions, and provide cost-to-serve inputs.
  + Drive proactive exception management for constrained inventory, customer allocation decisions, backorder risk, order holds, shipment readiness, and cross-functional communication.
* **Customer Service**
  + Lead day-to-day customer service for wholesale, retail, distributor, and eCommerce accounts, serving as the operational link between Chomps' fulfillment network and its customers. Oversee order status and shipment inquiries, the shared Customer Service inbox, and open-order review, catching PO issues (pricing errors, MOQ shortfalls, unapproved NetSuite POs, missed ship-by dates) before shipment.
  + Set the team's structure and standards, including priorities, ownership boundaries, escalation paths, channel coverage, backup plans, a shared tracker, and an SOP library. Define and monitor KPIs such as inbox response time, on-time weekly PO updates, PO issue resolution time, OTIF, and fill rate.
  + Serve as the primary supply chain point of contact for key customers, supporting business reviews and new-customer onboarding. Partner with Sales, Account Management, Planning, and Quality to resolve customer issues and deliver weekly PO status updates, cut and delay notices, post-allocation ETAs, key-account update files, and customer portal PO approvals.
  + Own processes for PO revisions, cancellations, and expedites; UDRs, shortages, damages, and returns; and chargebacks, deductions, and disputes, with clear ownership from intake through resolution. Manage retailer compliance (routing guides, vendor manuals, labeling mandates, ASN accuracy, EDI readiness, and appointment scheduling) to protect OTIF and minimize penalties.
  + Turn customer feedback and performance trends into process improvements, driving root-cause analysis and corrective action with 3PLs, carriers, and internal teams to reduce chargebacks, shorten PO-to-delivery cycle time, and manage cost-to-serve. Partner with Planning on retailer demand signals, In-Stock %, Weeks of Supply, and CPFR with key accounts.
* **Technology, Reporting & KPIs**
  + Support business-side execution of order management and fulfillment automation improvements, including reducing manual touches, improving order accuracy, strengthening exception workflows, supporting UAT, driving adoption, and increasing visibility across systems and 3PL partners.
  + Partner with Digital Transformation, Business Analytics, Sales Operations, and 3PL technology teams on NetSuite and partner-system improvements, including requirements, EDI/API integrations, order routing logic, reporting, issue tracking, and operational controls.
  + Own fulfillment scorecards and KPI reporting across service, cost, compliance, productivity, inventory flow, automation adoption, customer requirements, and partner performance, converting recurring issues into corrective action plans, partner follow-up, leadership-ready updates, and prioritized improvement recommendations.
  + Build ad hoc analyses that identify service risks, cost drivers, recurring partner issues, customer compliance exposure, inventory constraints, and opportunities for process improvement.
* **Launch Readiness**
  + Manage operational readiness for fulfillment, ensuring 3PL processes, documentation flows, lot traceability, shipment readiness, customer requirements, and exception management are defined and consistently executed.
  + Coordinate operational launch readiness for new customers, channels, facilities, lanes, and market launches by confirming people, processes, systems, inventory, documentation, partner capabilities, and escalation paths are aligned before go-live.
* **People & Cross-Functional Leadership**
  + Guide, coach, and develop customer service and fulfillment team members as applicable, and influence cross-functional stakeholders, by reinforcing clear ownership, operating rhythms, priorities, and expectations and building a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and disciplined follow-through.
  + Partner with cross-functional teams and external partners to align on execution priorities, resolve constraints, and support fulfillment growth.
  + Translate business growth priorities into practical execution plans, partner requirements, system needs, process controls, and team readiness actions.
  + Provide operational insights, data-backed recommendations, implementation support, and disciplined follow-through to support leadership decisions related to network planning, transportation, contracts, budgets, partner performance, and risk response.

**Who You Are**

* 7+ years of progressive experience in fulfillment, distribution planning, customer supply chain, logistics, or 3PL operations, including experience managing complex multi-node distribution networks and customer-facing operational process.
* Demonstrated ability to manage 3PL partners, operational KPIs, QBRs, corrective actions, SLA follow-up, and fulfillment performance across multiple facilities or business channels.
* Experience with ERP, WMS, TMS, EDI, API, and order management systems; NetSuite experience strongly preferred.
* Proven ability to identify, design, and implement automation or process improvement opportunities that improve order accuracy, reduce manual work, accelerate cycle times, and strengthen operational visibility.
* Highly analytical and comfortable using data to make recommendations on allocation, cost-to-serve, service risk, inventory positioning, readiness gaps, and partner performance.
* Strong understanding of fulfillment and supply chain metrics, including OTIF, fill rate, order cycle time, inventory accuracy, warehouse productivity, cost-per-order or cost-per-case, 3PL SLA performance, chargeback exposure, and capacity utilization.
* Strong cross-functional leadership skills with the ability to influence Sales, Planning, Finance, Operations, Quality, Digital Transformation, and external partners without always having direct authority.
* Comfortable operating at both planning and execution levels, moving from operational readiness and issue resolution to SOP development, partner follow-up, and process improvement.
* Excellent written and verbal communicator with the ability to translate operational complexity into clear recommendations, leadership-ready updates, and partner-facing expectations.
* Entrepreneurial, proactive, and process-oriented; energized by building scalable systems, improving ways of working, and creating structure in a high-growth environment.
* Demonstrated p[eople leadership experience, including coaching, prioritization, ownership setting, and development of team members.
* Willingness to travel up to 30% to distribution centers, partner sites, customer meetings, and cross-functional business reviews.

Title: Head of Enterprise Architecture
Description:
Medica is a nonprofit health plan with more than a million members that serves communities in Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Missouri, and beyond. We deliver personalized health care experiences and partner closely with providers to ensure members are genuinely cared for.

We're a team that owns our work with accountability, makes data-driven decisions, embraces continuous learning, and celebrates collaboration — because success is a team sport. It's our mission to be there in the moments that matter most for our members and employees. Join us in creating a community of connected care, where coordinated, quality service is the norm and every member feels valued.

The Head of Enterprise Architecture (HEA) is responsible for establishing and leading Medica's enterprise architecture organization and ensuring Medica’s enterprise architecture aligns and enables, our business strategy, operating capabilities, technology, data, and processes, resulting in measurable and increasing enterprise value. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, the HEA serves as a strategic advisor to the CIO and senior business and technology leaders and leads a multidisciplinary architecture organization spanning enterprise, business, security, data, integration, and related architecture disciplines. The HEA also leads an enterprise-wide Architecture Community of Practice to align architects and architecture-adjacent roles around common principles, standards, methods, patterns, and decision practices.

Business Architecture is a foundational discipline of the practice. The HEA ensures a clear understanding of enterprise business objectives, the current and required state of business capabilities, and the value-aligned roadmaps needed to move from current to target state. These roadmaps integrate changes across technology, data, processes, organization, skills, and operating models. The role partners closely with the Office of the CIO, Enterprise Transformation, Business Process Re-engineering, Product Ownership, Engineering, Data, Security, and business leadership to translate strategy into executable change.

The HEA will evolve Enterprise Architecture from a traditional, centralized governance model toward an enabling, embedded, and delivery-oriented practice. Architecture will engage earlier and more deeply in strategic and day-to-day delivery, using reusable standards, reference architectures, patterns, guardrails, and risk-based decision frameworks to accelerate sound decisions. The HEA will also advance AI-enabled architecture practices to automate routine documentation, analysis, standards validation, knowledge management, and governance activities so architects can focus on solving critical business problems, transformation, complex design decisions, and delivery enablement.

**Key Accountabilities**

**Structure and Advance Enterprise Architecture Practices**

* Establish and continuously evolve the enterprise architecture strategy, operating model, principles, standards, methods, and practices.
* Establish Business Architecture as the connective layer between enterprise strategy, transformation, product portfolios, business processes, organizational design, data, and technology.
* Ensure development and maintenance of enterprise business capability models; partner to assess current-state maturity and identify capability gaps, dependencies, duplication, and investment needs.
* Translate enterprise strategy and business objectives into target states, transition states, and value-aligned capability roadmaps integrating changes to people, process, technology, data, organization, skills, and operating models.
* Provide enterprise leaders with clear views of strategic dependencies, tradeoffs, sequencing, technical health, and investment implications.
* Ensure technology strategy is traceable to business strategy and capability requirements.

**Deliver Enterprise Transformation & Strategy through Architecture**

* Serve as a strategic architecture advisor to the CIO, executive leadership, Transformation, Product, and business leaders.
* Partner with Enterprise Transformation and Business Process Re-engineering to connect strategic objectives, transformation portfolios, and process redesign to required business-capability changes.
* Partner with Product Owners and Product Management to connect enterprise capability roadmaps with product strategies, investment priorities, and delivery roadmaps.
* Ensure architecture strategy reflects the operating, regulatory, data, and interoperability requirements of a healthcare organization, with particular emphasis on the health plan/payer environment.
* Provide architectural leadership for healthcare interoperability and industry standards, including X12 EDI, HL7 FHIR, USCDI, and other applicable healthcare information-exchange standards.
* Translate regulatory and interoperability requirements into enterprise capabilities and strategic roadmaps in partnership with Compliance, Legal, Security, Privacy, Product, Data, and business leaders.

**Architecture Enablement & Governance**

* Modernize the Architecture Review process from a primarily centralized approval mechanism into a risk-based architecture enablement model embedded earlier in strategy, discovery, design, and delivery.
* Establish reference architectures, reusable patterns, standards, guardrails, decision frameworks, and architecture decision records that increase delivery autonomy while maintaining enterprise alignment.
* Define clear decision rights across Enterprise Architecture, domain architecture, solution architecture, Engineering, Product, Security, Data, and related functions.
* Partner with engineering and technology leaders to evaluate and select strategic platforms, core technologies, architectural patterns, and engineering approaches.
* Guide modernization of core capabilities including Cloud, APIs, integration, data platforms, automation, AI, SaaS, and digital capabilities while reducing unnecessary complexity, duplication, and technical debt.
* Use AI and automation to improve architecture knowledge discovery, documentation, standards validation, impact analysis, dependency identification, and governance workflows, freeing architects for higher-value work.
* Measure architecture effectiveness through business outcomes, delivery enablement, reuse, simplification, risk reduction, technology health, and decision quality.

**Architecture Team Leadership**

* Lead, develop, and mentor a multidisciplinary architecture organization spanning enterprise, business, security, data, integration, and related architecture disciplines.
* Establish and lead an enterprise-wide Architecture Community of Practice encompassing architects and architecture-adjacent roles across centralized and distributed teams.
* Define common architecture principles, terminology, methods, artifacts, modeling approaches, standards, and expectations across the organization.
* Create mechanisms for knowledge sharing, reusable solutions, emerging practices, and lessons learned across the architecture community.
* Develop architecture talent, competency models, career paths, succession plans, and leadership capability across the enterprise.
* Build an architecture culture based on influence, transparency, collaboration, practical guidance, and accountability rather than centralized control.
* Operate effectively from executive strategy through delivery-level architecture, communicating complex business and technology concepts to technical and nontechnical audiences.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* 15+ years of progressively responsible experience across enterprise technology, architecture, business transformation, engineering, or related disciplines; significant leadership experience building and leading enterprise or domain architecture functions in complex organizations.
* 5+ years of people management experience leading highly technical roles in direct, indirect, and contractor roles.
* Business capability modeling and capability-based planning; strategy-to-execution alignment; value-stream and operating-model analysis; enterprise transformation and roadmap development; architecture governance and operating models; modern cloud, API, integration, data, security, SaaS, automation, and AI architectures; healthcare interoperability; executive communication, facilitation, organizational change, stakeholder influence, and talent development

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Masters degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related discipline preferred.
* Experience managing vendor relationships.
* Healthcare payer / managed care experience strongly preferred; broader healthcare experience considered.

Description:
Questrade is on a mission to help Canadians to become much more financially successful and secure.

*This job posting is for an existing vacancy.*

**We're looking for our next Senior Manager, JSOC & Threat Hunting**

The Senior Manager, JSOC & Threat Hunting is a hands-on technical leader accountable for security monitoring, incident response, threat hunting and intelligence, detection and security engineering, vulnerability management and DevSecOps across Questrade Financial Group's regulated entities. She/he leads the Joint Security Operations Centre (JSOC) as a 24x7, multi-shift operation spanning three teams (SOC and Incident Response, Threat Operations and Engineering, and DevSecOps), owns the JSOC service catalogue, and remains directly involved in major incidents, complex investigations, detection design, SIEM optimization and security tooling decisions. This is not a coordination-only leadership role. The role operates in a dual regulatory environment covering CIRO regulated dealer and wealth entities and OSFI regulated federal financial institutions, and is the senior escalation point for cyber incident detection, containment and the incident inputs required for regulator reporting.

**The mandate**

In this role, you will:

* Lead the Joint Security Operations Centre as a highly technical, hands-on leader across three teams: SOC and Incident Response, Threat Operations and Engineering, and DevSecOps. Remain directly involved in complex investigations, high-severity incidents, detection design, SIEM optimization and security tooling decisions, and challenge technical assumptions rather than rely on tool-generated conclusions.
* Own and maintain the JSOC service catalogue across three service lines (SOC/IR, Threat Operations, and DevSecOps), with defined service levels, a named owner and a named backup for every service line.
* Run alert monitoring and response as a continuous, multi-shift operation across five countries, ensuring coverage, shift handover discipline and consistent investigation quality across regions and time zones.
* Own the incident management lifecycle end to end, including severity classification, escalation paths, playbooks, evidence handling and chain of custody, containment, remediation, recovery and lessons learned. Provide technical direction from triage through closure on major incidents and lead cross-functional coordination with engineering, infrastructure, cloud, identity, fraud, privacy, legal and business teams.
* Ensure incident detection, classification and evidence are sufficient to meet OSFI technology and cyber security incident reporting expectations, including the 24-hour initial notification, and CIRO cybersecurity incident reporting obligations. Label every incident to the correct entity and regime and provide timely, accurate inputs to the Global Security Office, Legal, Privacy and Compliance.
* Oversee the design, testing, tuning and lifecycle management of detection rules and alerts mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Improve SIEM effectiveness by reducing noise and false positives, optimising queries and ensuring alerts are actionable, and maintain a measured view of detection coverage and known gaps.
* Develop and run a proactive threat hunting program covering employee-facing and client-facing threats, informed by threat intelligence, attacker behaviours, environmental risk and observed detection gaps. Convert hunt findings into durable detections and control improvements.
* Own CTI tooling configuration, alert set-up, monitoring and response, and feed intelligence into detection, hunting, vulnerability prioritisation and fraud use cases.
* Own enterprise vulnerability management and external attack surface management, including EASM configuration and inventory, prioritisation by exploitability and entity exposure, and remediation tracking with named owners and committed dates in partnership with technology owners.
* Provide technical leadership for Elastic Security, including log source onboarding, parsing and configuration, data ingestion, query development, dashboards, detection rules, integrations and platform optimisation. Ensure logging and telemetry across applications, APIs, endpoints, identity systems, networks, cloud platforms and third-party services provide the visibility required to detect and investigate activity.
* Own deployment, administration and lifecycle management of JSOC security solutions, including Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA, ZDX) and email security, and evaluate and improve tools, integrations and workflows on measurable operational value.
* Direct security and fraud research and development within the JSOC, including AI-assisted triage and automation, in line with enterprise AI governance requirements. Apply change control and independent review before any internally built tooling enters production, maintaining segregation between building a control and monitoring it.
* Lead the DevSecOps team in SAST and DAST configuration, application vulnerability management and application security advisory, prioritised by regulated-entity exposure. Partner with engineering and platform teams to integrate security controls and testing into CI/CD pipelines, investigate application-layer threats and strengthen detection across the software development lifecycle.
* Support integrity investigations for Compliance, HR, Fraud and Legal under evidence-handling standards, and partner with Enterprise Fraud on account takeover, abuse and fraud-adjacent detection and response affecting online financial services.
* Define and monitor operational metrics including detection coverage, alert quality, time to detect and respond, investigation outcomes, recurring incident patterns and control gaps, and prepare quarterly executive and Board committee reporting content for the Global Security Office.
* Participate in and facilitate incident simulations, technical tabletop exercises and post-incident reviews, ensuring lessons result in concrete improvements to controls, detections and response procedures.
* Hire, coach, develop and manage the JSOC leadership layer and, through them, the wider team. Raise the team's technical depth, set clear expectations for investigation quality and operational ownership, and manage span of control, shift staffing and succession so that no service line depends on a single person.
* Partner with Cyber Strategy, Risk and GRC, Offensive Security, Identity and Access Management, Enterprise Fraud, Enterprise Architecture, Cloud and Infrastructure, Privacy, Legal, Internal Audit and entity compliance officers. Provide evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF and regulator reviews covering detection and response controls.
* Review complex technical findings and communicate business impact, evidence and recommended actions clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including executive and Board committee audiences.
* Stay current with attacker techniques, application security risks, security operations practices, cloud-native security operations and technologies relevant to a Canadian regulated financial group.

**You're ready for this mandate if you have the following qualifications**

* 10+ years of relevant cybersecurity experience, including substantial experience in security operations, incident response, detection engineering or threat hunting, with 5+ years leading technical security professionals and at least 2 years leading managers or team leads.
* Strong hands-on incident response experience, including investigation, scoping, containment, remediation, recovery and post-incident analysis, with major incident leadership in a regulated financial services environment.
* Demonstrated experience running a 24x7 or follow-the-sun security operations function across multiple countries and shifts.
* Demonstrated experience conducting threat hunts and converting findings into durable detections or security improvements.
* Deep knowledge of SIEM operations, including alert development, query optimisation, data onboarding, false-positive reduction and detection coverage measurement.
* Strong practical experience with Elastic Security, Elasticsearch, Kibana, Elastic Query Language (EQL) and Kibana Query Language (KQL), or equivalent query and detection capabilities.
* Solid understanding of application security concepts, including common web and API attack techniques, secure development practices, vulnerability management and application-layer telemetry.
* Strong knowledge of endpoint, network, identity, cloud and application security data sources, and the ability to analyse logs, network activity, authentication events, endpoint telemetry and application behaviour without relying solely on tool-generated conclusions.
* Experience with MITRE ATT&CK and the Cyber Kill Chain, and with developing security automation, scripts, integrations or repeatable investigation workflows.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical risk clearly, make sound decisions in high-pressure situations and present to executive and Board committee audiences.
* A leadership style grounded in technical credibility, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement, with proven ability to build a leadership layer and manage span of control across a geographically distributed team.
* Experience in a regulated financial services environment such as banking, brokerage, wealth management, payments or fintech.
* CISSP, GCIH, GCIA, GCFA, GNFA, OSED, CPTS, Security+ or equivalent practical experience.
* Familiarity with OSFI B-13, B-10 and E-21, OSFI technology and cyber security incident reporting expectations and CIRO cybersecurity incident reporting obligations, or demonstrated ability to learn a new prudential regime quickly.
* Deep expertise with Zscaler products, including ZIA, ZPA, ZDX and related integrations and telemetry.
* Familiarity with CrowdStrike Falcon, Wiz, Aikido and cloud-native security operations in Google Cloud Platform or another major cloud provider.
* Experience integrating security controls and testing into CI/CD pipelines, and familiarity with SOAR platforms and AI-assisted triage and automation workflows.
* Experience investigating fraud, account takeover, abuse or other threats affecting online financial services.
* Experience with scripting or development in Python, JavaScript, Bash or another relevant language.

**Additional Information**

* Lead a globally distributed team operating a follow-the-sun model across Canada, Brazil, Armenia, Israel and Argentina, with shift-based SOC coverage (Shifts A, B and C) and flexible Eastern Time coverage.
* Working day anchored to the Toronto Eastern Time business day for executive, entity, auditor and regulator-facing engagement.
* Available for major incident escalation outside business hours, with a named deputy arrangement in place for planned absences so that incident command never depends on a single person.

Through enterprise programs, tools, and partnerships, the team helps leaders and teams strengthen connection, belonging, ownership, and performance; embed desired ways of working into the everyday coworker experience, and build the capabilities needed to turn culture into a driver of business outcomes.

The Senior Manager, Joy & Listening Strategy is responsible for leading PG&E’s enterprise Joy at Work listening, measurement, and improvement strategy to advance the coworker experience and drive achievement of the enterprise Joy at Work L1 metric. This role oversees the collection, analysis, and translation of coworker feedback into actionable insights, strategic priorities, and measurable improvements, with a particular focus on frontline coworkers and organizations with the greatest opportunity for improvement.
  
  
The Senior Manager provides strategic leadership and oversight of enterprise listening programs, including but not limited to Joy at Work surveys, Joy Pulse and Joy Daily, ensuring a coordinated approach to measuring coworker sentiment, identifying key performance drivers, and evaluating the effectiveness of improvement actions. This role leads a team of analysts and program professionals and partners with functional area leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen accountability, accelerate improvement and embed data-informed decision-making into enterprise operating rhythms.
  
  
The role is hybrid working from your remote office and in-person at Oakland General Office, 1-2x weekly based on business needs.
  
  
Job Responsibilities
  
Lead the development and execution of PG&E’s enterprise Joy at Work listening and measurement strategy, establishing priorities, performance expectations and improvement opportunities that drive achievement of the enterprise L1 Joy at Work metric. Partner with functional areas to identify performance gaps, evaluate improvement plans, and accelerate progress toward enterprise targets. Oversee the enterprise listening ecosystem, including Joy at Work surveys, Joy Pulse, Joy Daily and other feedback mechanisms. Establish consistent approaches to collecting, analyzing, and interpreting coworker sentiment, ensuring insights are timely, actionable, and connected to enterprise priorities. Develop targeted listening and measurement strategies that elevate frontline coworker perspectives, address participation and accessibility barriers, and identify opportunities to improve the frontline experience. Partner with operational leaders to translate frontline insights into prioritized improvement actions and measurable outcomes. Direct the analysis of Joy performance drivers, sentiment trends, and coworker feedback to inform enterprise priorities and leadership decisions. Establish consistent methods to evaluate the effectiveness of functional area Joy improvement plans, recommend adjustments, and strengthen the connection between listening, action, and results. Lead the integration of Joy insights and performance measures into enterprise operating rhythms, including Joy Councils, monthly operating reviews, leadership forums, and structured problem-solving. Establish clear performance expectations, escalation processes, and follow-up mechanisms to drive accountability and continuous improvement. Lead, coach, and develop a team of analysts and program professionals responsible for survey execution, data analytics, strategic insights, and program delivery. Partner with enterprise leaders, functional areas, and cross-functional teams to align priorities, strengthen execution and deliver measurable improvements in the coworker experience. Oversee complex and unique strategic planning projects and initiatives that are of highest visibility and impact. Create and implement long-term research and analytical strategies, ensuring effective execution to apply insights across product, marketing, customer, and integration strategies on a daily basis. Act as an advocate for coworkers to all areas of the Company. Lead identification of new and existing technologies and processes. Develop and manage budgets, across multiple funding sources and identify innovations and cost-reduction potential of new and existing technologies and processes and implement contract management process improvement.
  
  
Qualifications
  
  
**Minimum:**  
Bachelor’s Degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Economics, Statistics, or equivalent experience. 6 years of experience in utilities, retail, financial services, consumer products, or telecommunications including supervisory/managerial experience. 4 years’ experience in customer strategy work in the utility, financial services, telecommunications, or consumer products sectors.
  
  
**Desired Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  
Strong experience in implementing and using customer qualitative/quantitative research methods, tools, and applications of statistical analysis. Proven track record in defining strategic objectives and setting metrics and performance measures. Experience in successfully managing vendor relationships. Experience developing and implementing customer experience tools, i.e., journey maps, service blueprints, etc. Experience applying Lean methodology. Knowledge of concepts, best practices, tools, techniques, and strategies related to conducting behavioral analysis as needed to perform at the job level. Ability to read and understand information and ideas presented through written words and sentences as need to perform at the job level. Competency in developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. Ability to create graphics, maps, schematics, or diagrams to present information as needed to perform at the job level. Competency in making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. Competency in adapting approach and demeanor in real time to match the shifting demands of different situations. Competency in building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives. Knowledge of concepts, best practices, tools, techniques, and strategies related to intelligence data gathering, analysis, and decision-making as needed to perform at the job level.

Title: AIR FREIGHT PRICING AND OPERATIONS MANAGER
Description:
Air Freight Operations & Pricing Manager

**Company:** Unique Courier Cargo Services LLC  
**Location:** Dubai, UAE  
**Department:** Air Freight Operations & Pricing  
**Position Level:** Senior Management  
**Reports To:** Directors & Management

Job Overview

Unique Courier Cargo Services LLC is seeking a **highly experienced, commercially driven, and result-oriented Air Freight Operations & Pricing Manager** to take complete ownership of the company's air freight operations, pricing, airline relationships, and business development opportunities.

We are looking for a strong leader with extensive knowledge of international air freight, transshipment operations, airline pricing, and CMC (Cargo Mega Terminal) facilities and their potential business opportunities.

The selected candidate must be capable of independently managing the entire operations and pricing team, maintaining strong airline relationships, maximizing enquiry conversions, ensuring operational excellence, and taking full accountability for departmental performance.

**This is an ownership-driven leadership position, not merely an operational supervisory role.**

Key Responsibilities

**1. Complete Operations Management & Accountability**

* Take full responsibility for the day-to-day performance of the Air Freight Operations and Pricing Department.
* Lead, supervise, train, and guide the entire operations and pricing team.
* Ensure every customer enquiry is properly reviewed, priced, followed up, and converted wherever commercially feasible.
* Take complete accountability for all enquiries, quotations, bookings, shipment execution, and operational escalations.
* Establish clear responsibilities, productivity standards, and performance expectations for each team member.
* Ensure timely shipment execution, accurate documentation, regulatory compliance, and effective coordination with all stakeholders.
* Independently resolve operational challenges and implement preventive measures.

**2. Airline Relationships & Pricing Management**

* Maintain excellent working relationships with major airlines, GSAs, cargo terminals, and handling agents.
* Negotiate competitive freight rates, special rates, allotments, and commercial arrangements.
* Possess strong knowledge of airline networks, routing options, capacity availability, and international cargo regulations.
* Develop effective pricing strategies to improve both conversion rates and gross profitability.
* Build direct relationships with airline decision-makers to secure commercially advantageous opportunities.
* Continuously monitor market rates, competitor pricing, and airline developments.

**3. Transshipment & CMC Business Development**

* Demonstrate extensive knowledge of international cargo transshipment operations through Dubai and other major hubs.
* Identify and develop business opportunities involving CMC facilities, cargo consolidation, transit cargo, and cross-border freight movements.
* Develop commercially viable solutions for cargo movements through Dubai, including documentation, handling, routing, and regulatory requirements.
* Establish relationships with international freight forwarding agents and overseas business partners.
* Identify new trade lanes, airline partnerships, and transshipment business opportunities.
* Present practical business development proposals to management, including revenue potential, expected margins, operational requirements, and implementation plans.

**4. Enquiry Management & 95% Conversion Target**

* Drive the department toward a **target of 95% conversion of qualified, commercially viable enquiries**.
* Ensure 100% of enquiries are recorded, assigned, monitored, and followed up.
* Implement a structured quotation and follow-up system to minimize lost business.
* Analyze unsuccessful quotations and identify the reasons for lost business.
* Ensure quotations are competitive, accurate, profitable, and delivered within established turnaround times.
* Work closely with the Sales Department to convert enquiries into confirmed shipments.
* Take ownership of improving enquiry quality, quotation efficiency, customer retention, and shipment volumes.

**5. Weekly Management Reporting**

Submit a detailed weekly performance report to management covering:

* Total enquiries received, quotations submitted, and shipments confirmed.
* Enquiry conversion percentage and comparison against the 95% target.
* Total sales revenue and gross profit generated.
* Shipment volumes, chargeable weight, and major trade lanes.
* Lost enquiries, reasons for non-conversion, and corrective actions.
* Airline rate developments and negotiated commercial benefits.
* Individual team performance, productivity, and accountability.
* Operational issues, shipment delays, and resolutions.
* New business opportunities, particularly in transshipment and CMC operations.
* Action plan for the coming week with measurable targets.

The Manager must be able to **explain departmental performance, identify shortcomings, and present actionable solutions rather than merely report figures.**

**6. Leadership & Professional Representation**

* Represent the company professionally in meetings with airlines, customers, international agents, and business partners.
* Maintain excellent personal presentation, professional grooming, communication, and business etiquette.
* Demonstrate confidence, strong negotiation capabilities, commercial awareness, and sound decision-making.
* Conduct regular departmental performance meetings and ensure effective team coordination.
* Develop employees through training, mentoring, and practical operational guidance.
* Demonstrate leadership through ownership, discipline, accountability, and consistent performance.
* Act as the primary escalation point for air freight operational and pricing matters.

Candidate Requirements

* Minimum **8–10 years of relevant experience** in air freight forwarding, operations, and pricing, preferably within the UAE market.
* At least 3–5 years in a managerial or senior leadership position.
* Established professional relationships with airlines, GSAs, and air cargo handling agents in the UAE.
* Strong expertise in transshipment operations, Dubai air cargo facilities, CMC-related opportunities, and cargo handling procedures.
* Excellent knowledge of import, export, transit cargo, customs procedures, AWB documentation, and airline regulations.
* Working knowledge of IATA regulations, dangerous goods procedures, and international freight forwarding practices.
* Proven ability to negotiate competitive airline rates and develop profitable freight solutions.
* Demonstrated experience managing operational teams and improving enquiry conversion rates.
* Strong analytical, reporting, communication, and commercial negotiation skills.
* Excellent command of English, both written and spoken.
* Professional appearance, leadership presence, and ability to represent the company at senior-level meetings.
* Ability to work independently, take ownership, and deliver measurable results with minimal supervision.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)Performance AreaExpected TargetEnquiry accountability100% enquiries tracked and assignedEnquiry conversion95% of qualified, commercially viable enquiriesQuotation turnaroundWithin approved service-specific timelinesWeekly reporting100% on-time submissionOperational executionMinimum delays and avoidable errorsGross profitConsistent monthly growth against approved targetsAirline relationshipsCompetitive rates and measurable commercial improvementsTransshipment businessNew profitable opportunities and confirmed shipmentsTeam managementClear accountability, training, and continuous improvementCustomer satisfactionTimely resolutions and professional serviceManagement Expectations

The successful candidate will be expected to operate with the mindset of a **Department Head and Business Leader**, taking responsibility not only for completing shipments but also for building a highly efficient, profitable, and commercially competitive Air Freight Department.

Management expects someone who can independently identify problems, provide solutions, generate opportunities, develop the team, and deliver measurable improvements in operational performance and profitability.

**We are looking for a strong, decisive, hands-on leader who takes complete ownership of the department, builds lasting airline relationships, drives business growth, and is accountable for results.**

Title: Director, Project Management
Description:
Everest Clinical Research (“Everest”) is a full-service contract research organization (CRO) providing a broad range of expertise-based clinical research services to worldwide pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries. We serve some of the best-known companies and work with many of the most advanced drugs, biologics, and medical devices in development today.

Everest has been an independent CRO since 2004 with a strong foundation as a statistical and data management center of excellence. Building on this foundation, Everest has successfully developed and established itself as a full-service CRO. Everest’s Corporate headquarters are located in Ontario, Canada and US headquarters in New Jersey, USA, with additional physical offices in Asia and Europe.

Everest is known in the industry for its high-quality deliverables, superior customer service, and flexibility in meeting clients’ needs. A dynamic organization with an entrepreneurial origin, Everest continues to experience exceptional growth and great success.

Quality is our backbone, customer-focus is our tradition, flexibility is our strength…that’s us…that’s Everest.

To drive continued success in this exciting clinical research field, we are seeking a committed, skilled, and customer-focused individual to join our winning team as a **Director, Project Management** for our Toronto/Markham, Ontario, Canada on-site location, or remotely from a home-based office anywhere in Canada in accordance with our Work from Home policy.

**Director, Project Management:**

This leadership role will oversee the project planning, communication, and execution of clinical research and development services offered by Everest. Direct reports include all levels and roles within the Project Management department, including Associate Directors, Senior Managers, Managers, Senior Project Managers, Project Managers, Associate Project Managers and Project Coordinators. In-direct reports/subordinates are those Project Managers who are assigned to the tasks on the client studies and projects overseen by the Director of Project Management (matrixed organization).

**JOB ACCOUNTABILITIES:**

* Plan and implement new client service delivery requests within client portfolio; support evolution of existing client portfolio, providing holistic biometrics and full services (including clinical operations) project deliveries across multiple clinical development programs.
* Strategically align the efforts of functional area directors and managers in project planning, identification of tasks and deliverables, and assessment of resource needs and utilization for existing and new clients/sponsors.
* Perform project and portfolio performance tracking for responsible projects using strategic planning and project tracking methods and tools. Conduct regular project progress reviews with internal teams for assigned portfolios, and facilitate conduct of Everest and Client governance meetings to optimize partnership expectations and performance.
* Check and ensure that responsible projects carried out at Everest are properly tracked and managed according to Everest’s quality, operational and financial budget standards. Support solution and budget development for complex and unique projects and scope to address client requirements.
* Provide leadership, training, mentorship, and management oversight of project management staff. This may include mentorship and training of team members to deliver project management services for specific client portfolios, or mentorship and career development of individuals in a line management capacity.
* In consultation with the senior Project Management leadership, review new Project Management Applicants and recommend hires for interview processing.
* In consultation with the senior Project Management leadership, further develop and establish policies and Standard Operating Procedures in project management for assurance of quality deliverables. Continue to support the development, update, and review of governing documents and WIs for the department.
* Initiate, drive, and support project management departmental process and technology improvement initiatives. Lead and contribute to developing reusable project management templates and training materials that can be used to improve effectiveness and efficiency of project delivery by other team members.
* Through the periodic project/portfolio review meetings, effectively identify issues such as lack of planning, lack of resources, poor team performance, or other external factors negatively impacting the ongoing projects, and bring the issues and solutions to the attention of the functional area directors and managers. Work with the functional area directors and managers to jointly ensure smooth project starting up, continuation, and successful completion.
* In consultation with Everest functional leaders and senior project management leadership, interact with clients for strategic partnership governance activities, which includes but is not limited to project pipeline and delivery planning, measuring performance metrics for the portfolio, identifying new project/service opportunities within the existing portfolio, implementing performance improvement and innovation initiatives, and obtaining key information to aid in the projection of resource requirements and project management purposes.
* Manage all project management aspects of assigned Phase I -IV clinical trials and in accordance with ICH guidelines, FDA, Health Canada, EMA, and other applicable regulatory and legal requirements.
* Lead cross-functional project teams. Manage the planning, implementation, conduct, and reporting of assigned projects within the established timelines and budgets, and with the quality and requirements necessary for regulatory approvals.
* Proactively track and manage project tasks against timelines and hours spent/budgets, alert management when there are risks of having major deviations. Proactively track and manage the financial status against budget and reconcile expenses across sub-streams of activities.
* Function as senior level facilitator of problem solving and conflict resolution, and act as a 2nd level escalation resource.
* Conduct “lessons learned” meetings with project team members to learn from failures and prevent same from future projects.
* Contribute and/or participate in the performance evaluation of staff who performed under the responsible projects.
* When required, this position may assist the organization in responding to and preparing for RFI and RFPs, and subsequently leading and participating in bid defense meetings, defining work scopes and budgets, and leading contract administration activities.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* B.Sc. or M.Sc. in life sciences or health related field.
* A minimum of 18 years of experience in clinical research and development within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, institutional, or CRO setting.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop others within functional area.
* Demonstrated understanding of cross-functional processes including clinical operations, statistics, data management, pharmacovigilance, subject randomization and drug supply management, data monitoring and adjudication committees, regulatory affairs, and medical writing.
* Knowledge and understanding of ICH guidelines, FDA, Health Canada, and EMA regulations.
* Ability to define scopes and estimate budgets, plan and manage projects, including resource requirements and utilization, hours spent vs. budgets, key deliverables and timelines.
* Demonstrated leadership abilities, including setting goals for others and driving to achieve them in accordance with allocated resources, timelines, and budgets.
* Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills. Demonstrated strong negotiation and presentation skills.
* Strong ability in problem-solving, including conflict resolution.

  

**Benefits & Compensation:**

We offer a robust benefits package to support your health, well-being, and growth, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, life & AD&D insurance, short- and long-term disability, tuition reimbursement, fitness reimbursement, employee assistance program (EAP), a pension plan, generous paid time off and sick leave, and the opportunity to earn a performance based bonus.

To find out more about Everest Clinical Research and to review other opportunities, please visit our website at www.everestclinical.com (http://www.ecrscorp.com).

Estimated Salary Range: $190,000 - 240,000.

We thank all interested applicants, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities, and upon request we will provide accommodations for candidates participating in any part of our recruitment and selection process.

**Job Description**

The position will support both the technical practice and operational management of the Markham/Mississauga operation, with particular emphasis on project profitability, client satisfaction, effective project delivery, and efficient business operations.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

* Support the day-to-day operational management and performance of Buildings + Places in Markham and Mississauga.
* Work with leadership to implement business priorities and maintain consistent operational discipline across the local practice.
* Monitor project and business performance and identify areas requiring management attention or corrective action.
* Support project managers in maintaining strong financial performance, forecasting, cost control, profitability, and delivery discipline.
* Coordinate workload and resource planning to align available staff with current and anticipated project requirements.
* Monitor utilization, staffing requirements, and workload forecasts to identify capacity constraints, underutilization, and emerging resource needs.
* Work closely with project managers, technical leaders, project controls, and finance to improve visibility and accountability for project performance.

* Experience supporting the financial and operational performance of projects or a portfolio of projects.

* Experience with project financial performance, resource forecasting, utilization management, and operational reporting.

* Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across technical disciplines and business functions.

The Operations Manager will be a visible and engaged member of the Markham/Mississauga Buildings + Places team, providing practical operational support to project managers and technical leaders while reinforcing accountability for project performance and operational discipline.

Description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it's a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn't been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

* Creating a strategic roadmap and services architecture for how Scout Motors will sell and transact new and used vehicles to retail customers, from purchase through delivery.
* Supporting and driving the definition and design of the ideal transaction process from an operational perspective (documentation, information flows, and third-party integrations).
* Leading vehicle registration compliance efforts across all active and future sales markets, including program build-out, process design, and cross-functional enablement.
* Developing and documenting comprehensive knowledge of vehicle sales and registration requirements across all states, counties, and localities.
* Designing and operationalizing transaction and delivery workflows and an efficient operating model that ensures a scalable, reliable, customer-centric experience.
* Partnering closely with product managers and engineers to translate operational needs into requirements, prioritize improvements, and develop scalable tools and vendor integrations for end-to-end vehicle sales transactions and deliveries, including documentation, payments, financing, registration, and delivery readiness.
* Leading the operational implementation of AI and automation across the transaction and delivery journey, identifying practical use cases that reduce manual work, improve document accuracy, and help customers complete their purchase and prepare for delivery.
* Owning business testing, rollout, and team adoption of new tools, with clear escalation paths and appropriate human review; measuring impact on transaction completion time, accuracy, team productivity, and the customer experience to guide ongoing improvements.
* Creating a technical support model for sales transaction workflows and operating models.
* Coordinating with Finance to define and build systems that accurately recognize vehicle revenue, ensuring alignment between operations and financial reporting.
* Participating in vendor evaluations and providing operational insight for standard operating procedures, transaction policies, and retail training.
